ideas.title: Grossman-Zhou cushion Kelly on a 3-bucket risk-parity core, executed by daily largest-gap pair trades
ideas.sketch: Risky core: three macro buckets (Growth = US LC, US SC, Dev ex-US, EM, REITs; Nominal = Treasuries 7-10y, IG credit; Real = TIPS, gold, commodities), inverse-volatility within each bucket and equal risk contribution across buckets from a 120-day covariance of daily close returns, so no bucket exceeds 1/3 of core risk at any date. Total invested fraction follows the Grossman-Zhou growth-optimal rule under a drawdown constraint: f = min(1, (NAV - 0.82*HWM) / (NAV * L)), where L = 2.33 * sigma_core(60d) * sqrt(20) is a 1-in-100 twenty-day core loss floored at 6%; the remainder sits in uninvested cash, and the 2-point buffer below the 20% limit absorbs execution lag. Execution each trading day: compute target weights, sort per-ETF gaps, fill gaps that reduce total exposure first, then trade the largest overweight/underweight pairs until one-way turnover hits 4%, and if every gap is below 0.1% still trade the largest gap, so every trading day has a trade and weekly turnover is at most 5*4% = 20% by construction. The return mechanism is the diversified risk premia of three low-correlated buckets plus the rebalancing (diversification) return of about 0.5*(sum w_i*sigma_i^2 - sigma_p^2), with exposure mechanically cut as the cushion shrinks; in a 2008 or 2022 path, a 15% core loss over 20 days removes most of the cushion and the 4%/day de-risking lane reaches cash in at most 25 days, which should keep maximum drawdown near 18%.

ideas.title: Crisis-correlation risk parity: ERC on a stress-day covariance with per-asset trend gates and five weekday tranches
ideas.sketch: Estimate covariance only from stress days, defined as the 100 worst equal-weight 10-ETF daily returns in the trailing 500 days, and shrink it 50/50 toward the full-sample 500-day covariance; then solve equal risk contribution across all 10 ETFs on that matrix, so diversification is judged by how assets co-move in sell-offs. When stock-bond correlation turns positive, as in 2022, the stress matrix sees it within weeks and moves budget from Treasuries and IG toward gold, TIPS, commodities and cash, instead of trusting the 2000-2020 bond hedge. Per-asset trend gate: an ETF whose close is below its 200-day simple moving average has its ERC weight halved, and the freed weight goes to cash rather than to other assets, so no class inherits another's risk. The whole book is then scaled so that stress-covariance volatility equals 7% per year, with total weight capped at 100%. Capital is split into five weekday sleeves of 20% each; each sleeve rebalances fully to the current target on its own weekday, with its own turnover clipped proportionally at 20% of the sleeve, which gives trades on every trading day, at most 4% portfolio turnover per day and at most 20% per week, and a 5-day staggered response that averages out signal noise instead of fighting it.
